prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] 3D low-poly wallpaper copying Hokusai's print: composition, palette, subjects; deliver scene/index.html + result.json.

[action]
- Read print.jpg directly: identified it, counted boats, noted palette (Prussian deep/mid/steel blue, cream foam, tan hulls, grey haze around Fuji).
- Wrote `result.json`: `boats: 3`, `mountain: "Mount Fuji"`, plus source attribution.
- Built `scene/index.html` (314 lines, single file, no build step): three.js 0.170.0 via the allowed jsdelivr import map only. All geometry in code: animated heightfield sea with quantized color bands (woodblock look), swept curling great wave left with foam-claw blobs and spray particles, 3 boats (cargo boat left in trough, 2 passenger boats with rowers center-right and foreground), snow-capped Fuji low center-right between troughs, right swell ridge, cream/grey gradient sky. Gentle motion: swell undulation, boat bob/roll, drifting spray, pulsing foam, slow camera drift.
- Verified live in the provided browser: first screenshot exposed a back-face-culled sea (wrong triangle winding, sky showed through); fixed winding, sky gradient, claw placement; re-screenshotted to confirm. Closed the tab I opened.

[result] Final render matches the print at a glance: giant clawing wave left, three boats, Fuji in the gap, right white swell, correct palette. Syntax and JSON validated (`node --check`, `JSON.parse` both OK). Assumptions: boat count = 3 as the print shows; "gentle motion" = ambient loop, no user controls; caption overlay is optional chrome.

[next] None; deliverables are final. Known cosmetic limit: foam claws read as clustered blobs rather than the print's fractal fingers, an accepted low-poly simplification.

How I know it is right: I inspected the print myself (3 boats, Fuji), and I opened the delivered file in the target browser and screenshotted it twice, iterating on what the screenshots actually showed until the composition matched.
